messages:
jane_customer: hi team — we have a customer reporting intermittent long TTFB on streaming responses since ~yesterday afternoon. total time for non-streaming is normal, but streaming first-chunk sometimes spikes to 2–4s at p99. region: us-west-2, model: redwood-7b-streaming-v1, sdk: node 1.6. They say toggling streaming off removes the spike. example request id: req_abc123. can share logs if useful.

support_anne: thanks @jane_customer — sorry about that. can you paste a minimal repro curl or the SDK call you used? are they using SSE or http/2 streaming? also any proxy in front of the client?

jane_customer: repro curl (SSE):
```
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-streaming-v1","input":"<long prompt>","stream":true}'
```
If I change to "stream": false the first byte comes in ~120ms. With stream=true the first chunk TTFB jumps to ~2.3s for some requests. No customer-side proxies reported beyond Cloudflare.

eli_ops: assigning myself to repro. quick note — we've seen h2+envoy coalescing issues cause delayed initial flush if backend writes are sub-100byte until buffer fills. grabbing traces for req_abc123 now.

eli_ops: logs for req_abc123 (truncated):
```
[2026-03-14T18:02:19.321Z] request=req_abc123 received at runtime
[2026-03-14T18:02:19.335Z] model=open-llm flush scheduled (initial chunk) size_est=48 bytes
[2026-03-14T18:02:21.650Z] first_chunk_delivered request=req_abc123 latency_ms=2310
[2026-03-14T18:02:23.100Z] total_done latency_ms=4310
```
looks like runtime produced an initial small chunk quickly but it wasn't delivered to client until ~2.3s later. sending more traces to the thread.

maria_s: useful — that smells like proxy coalescing/buffering in the edge or customer's Cloudflare. two angles: 1) confirm transport (SSE vs h2) and buffer behavior, 2) mitigate by forcing either smaller flush intervals from runtime OR bypass streaming for that tenant until we fix.

support_anne: customer confirms Cloudflare + direct outbound. their traffic is mostly HTTP/2.

eli_ops: reproducer with client-side h2 (local): i can reproduce ~90% when I route through our staging envoy with default write coalescing. when I turn on envoy config `socket_options: { tcp_nodelay: true }` and `stream_flush_timeout_ms: 5` the first chunk arrives ~40–80ms. with default coalesce window (10–20ms + write buffering) the first chunk can be delayed if initial chunk < ~1KB.

maria_s: mitigation options (short term):
- customer workaround: set header `X-Prefer-Streaming: false` or use SDK param `stream=false` for latency-sensitive endpoints (will increase total token latency/cost but fixes TTFB).
- infra workaround: apply per-tenant routing to non-streaming variant for this account until we deploy a better fix (cheap and fast).
- runtime tweak: increase initial chunk size (aggregate more tokens before first flush) so the proxy sees a larger write and won't coalesce. downside: increases first compute-to-first-send time.

alex_g: long term we should tune edge proxy flush heuristics + implement adaptive flush in the runtime: if downstream indicates h2+envoy or we detect high coalescing, runtime could emit a forced NOP flush (zero-length chunk) or small 512B initial chunk to avoid waiting. also consider exposing a header `x-redwood-stream-flush-ms` customers can set.

eli_ops: tried forced NOP/heartbeat approach in staging: runtime writes a 16-byte keepalive frame earlier and envoy passes it through fast -> reduces observed TTFB to ~80ms in my test. potential risk: increases network chatter and might break some clients expecting strict SSE framing.

support_anne: can we safely offer NOP/heartbeat as an opt-in feature for customers behind proxies? maybe via tenant flag.

maria_s: yes, opt-in seems safe. quick plan:
1) short-term: offer header workaround and route this tenant to non-streaming if they need immediate SLA. support to communicate to customer.
2) mid-term (48–72h): deploy opt-in heartbeat/forced flush toggle in runtime + enable for this tenant. monitor p95/p99.
3) long-term: tune edge proxy defaults and implement detection so runtime decides flush strategy by downstream hints.

alex_g: ops notes for rollout: patch runtime + feature flag + small envoy config change for edge fleet. will coordinate canary in us-west-2 only. need oncall windows.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT-2026-03-14-47 created: streaming-ttfb-edge-coalescing (owner=@eli_ops, priority=high) :clipboard:

eli_ops: action items assigned:
- collect a bucket of affected request ids (done, uploading to shared drive)
- create a small staging runtime build with heartbeat flush (PR up)
- smoke canary in us-west-2 and measure p95/p99 for first_chunk_latency

jane_customer: thanks — can we get the header workaround details to share with our engineering team? they'd prefer not to disable streaming permanently.

support_anne: sure — header: `X-Prefer-Streaming: false` OR SDK: `client.generate({..., stream: false})`. temporary routing: we'll flip them to non-streaming in us-west-2 if they want immediate relief; otherwise we can enable heartbeat feature for them in ~24-48h.

maria_s: noting customer FAQ blurb: "If you see high TTFB on streaming responses, try switching to non-streaming or contact support to enable an opt-in heartbeat flush while we tune proxies." add to KB after we close this.

eli_ops: monitoring notes: before fix p99 first_chunk_latency=3.6s, after heartbeat patch in staging p99 drops to 180ms, p95 ~95ms. will open canary dashboard and post link here when ready.

support_anne: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source. tagging @alex_g for rollout schedule and @maria_s for customer comms. :thumbsup:

alex_g: plan to canary tonight 02:00 UTC in us-west-2, small percentage. if green, roll out global over 6h. I'll post status updates in this thread.

eli_ops: uploaded repro and raw traces to /shared/support/1967890123/req_traces.tar.gz

jane_customer: appreciate the quick turnaround. please keep me posted, I'll pause the escalation if the header + non-streaming temp route is applied.

support_anne: marking follow-ups: (1) enable header workaround for customer (2) flip non-streaming route if requested (3) canary heartbeat today (4) KB article draft. I'll update when we flip route.

alex_g: update: canary started at 02:05 UTC — first_chunk p99 for canary <= 220ms. continuing ramp.

eli_ops: update 02:40 UTC — canary steady, no regressions in cpu or mem. rolling to 25% now.

alex_g: update 04:10 UTC — global rollout complete. monitoring shows p99 first_chunk down from 3.6s -> 210ms for affected tenants. closing incident after 2h steady.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT-2026-03-14-47 resolved by @alex_g (runtime heartbeat + edge tuning)

support_anne: customer notified and KB draft started here: /docs/kb/streaming-ttfb-mitigation.md

jane_customer: confirmed latency improved for our users. thanks all! :tada:
